snippet.title: Why My Mom Lives in Memory Care | The Realities of Dementia Caregiving 💜
snippet.description:
Teachable Moment: 

I know you don't mean any harm when CONSTANTLY asking but some things are hurtful anyway. DO YOU KNOW HOW HARD IS IT TO WATCH A PARENT WITH DEMENTIA LIVE IN MEMORY CARE? I know I make it look easy but it's NOT. 

Here are some things you should know since the question is such a HOT TOPIC: 

💜 1. Dementia Is Unpredictable
One moment everything seems fine, the next it can turn into aggression, confusion, or unsafe behavior. Memory care provides structure, trained staff, and an environment designed to keep them safe​ in a LOCKED facility.

💜 2. Safety Comes First
Falls, wandering, aggression, and medical needs are real risks. At home, it’s often impossible to provide 24/7 supervision without sacrificing the caregiver’s health. Memory care facilities are designed to reduce those risks.

💜 3. Caregivers Deserve Peace Too

Family members cannot live in constant chaos. Everyone deserves peace. Memory care can restore balance and protect everyone’s mental, emotional, and physical well-being.

💜 4. Violence Is Real
Not all people with dementia become violent — but some do. From being scratched, bitten, or hit, caregivers may endure abuse no one should have to tolerate at home. Memory care ensures both the parent and family remain safe.

💜 5. Love ​vs. Care
Placing a loved one in memory care is not ​ALWAYS abandonment — it’s an act of love. It means recognizing when their needs surpass what one person (or even a family) can provide, and choosing the best environment for their dignity, health, and freedom.​ I can love my mom to the moon and back but I cannot provide her the 24/7 CARE she requires and deserves. 

💜 6. Trained Professionals Are Essential
Memory care staff are trained in dementia behaviors, de-escalation, and medical monitoring. Even the most devoted family caregiver can’t replace a whole team of trained professionals available 24/7.

💜 7. Everyone’s Journey Is Different
There is no “one-size-fits-all” dementia journey. What works for one family may not work for another. Respect that every family has the right to choose what keeps their loved one safest and happiest.​ Remember, IT ALSO DEPENDS ON THE TEMPERMENT OF THE PERSON REQUIRING THE CARE! 

👉🏽 If this message resonates with you, please LIKE this video, SUBSCRIBE to the channel, and tap the notification bell 🔔 so you don’t miss future caregiving updates.
💬 Share your thoughts in the comments — have you ever been judged for your caregiving choices? Let’s support each other through this journey.
